$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.9,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.9/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 6b261c690b16017d8dfa4b736c4b6569abbc00e000c1b6b57e6f0253994c98b2 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.9/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
6b261c690b16017d8dfa4b736c4b6569abbc00e000c1b6b57e6f0253994c98b2 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
